purpose: The single machine-readable registry of what is true, what is contested, and what is ours. A coherence critic uses this file to tell a DELIBERATE in-world contradiction from a MISTAKE. If a contradiction is not in here, it is a mistake.

tier_definitions.hard-canon: Stated repeatedly and consistently across shipped Bethesda/ZOS material. The authorial world model obeys it. An in-world speaker may doubt it; narration may not.
tier_definitions.soft-canon: Stated once, or only by an unreliable in-world source, or era-scoped. We may take a side; the side must be registered.
tier_definitions.apocryphal: From a source the series itself marks unreliable. An in-world OPINION, never narration.
tier_definitions.constructed: Our invention. Binding on this project once written. Contradicting it is as much a failure as contradicting Bethesda.

provenance_definitions.community-data: Verified this session against a community-wiki summary returned by search. SECOND-HAND: a summary of a wiki summary of primary in-game text. Cite and re-verify when possible.
provenance_definitions.canonical-recall: Recalled from direct play/reading of the shipped games. Unverified.

verification_note: Direct fetches to en.uesp.net, elderscrolls.fandom.com, imperial-library.info and lagbt.wiwiland.net were all refused (HTTP 403 at the agent proxy gateway) on 2026-08-05. All 'community-data' entries rest on search-result summaries. An agent with unblocked access should re-verify CF-025, CF-044 and CF-050 before wave 2.

field_schema.id: CF-nnn hard/soft canon | CF-Dnnn disputed | CF-Cnnn constructed
field_schema.in_world_sources: books/NPCs in OUR game that assert this
field_schema.positions: [{id, in_world_source, stance, held_by[]}] — required when disputed
field_schema.deliberately_open: boolean — true means NO answer exists; never resolve it
field_schema.contradicts_ok: may our fiction contradict this? false = never

facts.claim: The Hist are giant sentient spore-trees native to Black Marsh, growing chiefly in the interior swamps.
sources_real: Pocket Guide to the Empire 3rd ed., Argonia

facts.claim: Argonian hatchlings drink Hist sap at hatching; the sap confers the hatchling's soul.
facts.notes: Load-bearing for the entire souls-as-levelling diegesis (RI-LOR05).

facts.claim: When an Argonian dies its soul returns to its Hist, is held there, and may be issued again to a later hatchling.
sources_real: UESP Lore:Hist (snippet): 'Argonian souls return to the Hist after death... the sap becomes the Argonian's blood, essence, and soul'
facts.notes: THE most load-bearing canon fact in this corpus. Bethesda built a souls-and-respawn metaphysics into Black Marsh and never made a game of it.

facts.claim: The Hist shapes Argonian bodies, deciding what hatches, and can reshape Argonians to meet need.
sources_real: Recurrent in ESO Murkmire and UESP Lore:Argonian
facts.notes: Anchor for levelling-as-regrowth. Because the Hist edits bodies, levelling is broad (attributes), not a score.

facts.claim: Hist sap carries the Hist's communication — visions, warning, summons — to an Argonian who drinks or licks it.
in_world_sources: The Sap and the Ledger (the flood anecdote)

facts.claim: Hist sap consumed by a NON-Argonian is a hallucinogen causing bloodlust; the drinker does not perceive what they are killing.
sources_real: Oblivion quest 'Infiltration'; UESP Lore:Blackwood Company (snippets) — the Water's Edge massacre
in_world_sources: A Practical Handling of the Marsh-Fevers, section 10
facts.notes: The entire sap-taint system rests on this. Softening it into a stat malus wastes hard canon.

facts.claim: Hist sap increases the combat prowess of those who drink it; Argonian shamans use it ritually.
The Hist say the Void is 'where all roots lead' and that they rejoin it; they speak of invoking the 'Songs of Sithis' in vengeance.
facts.notes: Attributed to the Hist THEMSELVES — in-world testimony, not narration.

facts.claim: During the Oblivion Crisis (3E 433+) the Hist withdrew the Argonians and organised a counter-invasion of the Deadlands so ferocious that Dagon's lieutenants sealed the gates.
facts.notes: AFTER our era. Never referenced in game. Establishes only that the Hist can act at continental scale when it chooses.

facts.claim: Argonians are reptilian, breathe water, and resist disease.
in_world_sources: Ledger and Journal of Andrel Vorin

facts.claim: Jel is the Argonian root-tongue; it runs on idiom and metaphor, is near-untranslatable without Black Marsh cultural knowledge, and forms words chiefly by compounding.
sources_real: UESP Lore:Jel; The Sharper Tongue: A Jel Primer (snippets)

facts.claim: Argonians carry both Jel names and Tamrielic names, the latter often direct translations of the former.
Hyphenated Tamrielic Argonian names may encode gender through the possessive (Lifts-Her-Tail, Hides-His-Eyes).
Attested Jel roots include beeko (friend), deelith (teacher), ku-vastei (needed change), xanmeer (stone-nest), lukiul (assimilated Argonian), kaoc (curse), thtithil (egg).
sources_real: The Sharper Tongue: A Jel Primer; UESP Lore:Shadowscales; UESP Lore:Ixtaxh Xanmeer (snippets)
facts.notes: RE-VERIFY FIRST. Glosses came from summaries, not the primer's own text.

facts.claim: The Naga are a scaled, serpentine Argonian form. Imperial sources characterise them as thugs responsible for banditry.
sources_real: UESP Lore:Naga; Pocket Guide 3rd ed. ('Argonian "Naga" thugs') (snippets)
facts.notes: The EXISTENCE of the Naga is hard canon; the 'thug' characterisation is Imperial contempt and must be depicted as such, never voiced as narration.

facts.claim: Argonians born under the sign of the Shadow are taken at birth and given to the Dark Brotherhood as Shadowscales; survivors to adulthood become full members.
Shadowscales may leave the Brotherhood to serve Black Marsh as ku-vastei — agents of needed change and arbiters who act with impunity.
facts.notes: A ready-made quest-giving institution with zero invention cost.

facts.claim: Duskfall ended the ancient high Argonian civilisation; the knowledge of how the xanmeers were built was lost with it and no living Argonian has it.

Xanmeers ('stone-nests') are pre-Duskfall Argonian stepped ziggurats, often in symmetrical complexes joined by elevated stone walkways, carved with geometric patterns and images of the ancient Argonians. Many are sunken or buried.
Many xanmeers are shrines erected in both reverence to and fear of Sithis; the purpose of many is lost.
facts.notes: Direct anchor for CF-C010, the soul-reservoir below the Stone Wastes.

facts.claim: Xanmeer names are Jel compounds, e.g. Ixtaxh-Thitithil-Meht ≈ 'Exact Egg-Cracker'.
The Ruddy Man is a figure of ancient Black Marsh legend associated with the deep past and a stone or ruddy body.
sources_real: UNVERIFIED — search this session returned no corroboration
facts.notes: DO NOT build load-bearing plot on this until verified. Low confidence; may be misremembered.

facts.claim: The Knahaten Flu began at Stormhold in 2E 560 and persisted 41 years, to 2E 601.
The Knahaten Flu drove the Kothringi and the Lilmothiit to extinction; Argonians were unaffected.
The Kothringi were silver-skinned humans native to Black Marsh, of Nedic descent, and notable sailors.
A small number of Kothringi survived the Flu 'through unnatural means'.
facts.notes: OPEN HOOK: one living Kothringi in 3E 427 is canon-legal and exactly the kind of impossible person Morrowind would have placed.

facts.claim: Blackrose prison was built by Potentate Versidae-Shae on the ruins of a Lilmothiit settlement called Blackrose.
sources_real: Partial corroboration in search snippet; primary source unverified
facts.notes: RE-VERIFY.

facts.claim: The Empire holds the coasts of Black Marsh and uses the interior for prisons; the heart of the province remains solely Argonian and is not under Imperial control.
sources_real: Pocket Guide to the Empire 3rd ed., Argonia (snippet)

facts.claim: House Dres of Morrowind has raided Black Marsh for slaves for centuries and slavery remains legal in Morrowind in 3E 427.
sources_real: UESP Lore:Black Marsh; Morrowind (3E 427) (snippets + shipped game)
in_world_sources: Ledger and Journal of Andrel Vorin
The Blessings of the Coast (denies it)
facts.notes: The era's central grievance. Must be depicted as CURRENT, never as history.

facts.claim: The Blackwood Company is a Leyawiin mercenary outfit, chiefly Khajiit and Argonian, that secretly doses its members with sap from a Hist kept in its hall cellar.
The An-Xileel formed during the Oblivion Crisis (3E 433+) and therefore DO NOT EXIST in 3E 427.
facts.notes: MOST LIKELY CANON BREAK. A builder searching 'Argonian faction' finds the wiki page and uses it. Naming them is an automatic 0.

facts.claim: REJECTED SOURCE: claims that Gideon is 'ruled by a Root-Assembly' and Blackrose 'governed by a Warden-Brood' originate from an AI-generated worldbuilding site (fables.gg), not from canon.
sources_real: fables.gg — REJECTED, non-canonical, do not re-import
facts.notes: Logged so no later agent re-imports it. Fluent, confident, entirely fabricated — the exact failure mode this registry exists to catch, encountered on day one.

facts.claim: Binding place names from the project map: Lilmoth, Soulrest, Blackrose, Gideon, Stormhold, Thorn, Archon, Helstrom; regions Valus Ridge, Blackwood, The Hive, Marauder's Coast, Stone Wastes, Western Rootlands, Eastern Rootlands, The Deep Marshes, The Stone Forest, The Clay Moor, Crimson Coast; waters Topal Bay, Padomaic Ocean.
facts.notes: No builder may rename, respell or 'improve' these. Helstrom is rendered on the map in an uncial face where H reads as b.

facts.claim: The interior of Black Marsh is functionally impassable to outsiders — no roads, shifting water, disease, and navigation by knowledge no foreigner has.
sources_real: Pocket Guide 3rd ed.; project map (tracks terminate at the coasts)
in_world_sources: A Practical Handling of the Marsh-Fevers

facts.claim: What survives when an Argonian soul returns to the Hist?
sources_real: Canon establishes the return (CF-003) but never adjudicates what persists.

positions.in_world_source: The Sap and the Ledger (Sergius Verrent)
positions.stance: The sap is a solvent. The individual dissolves into a common stock; what is issued to a new egg is MADE OF the dead, as a second loaf is made of the same flour. Argonians have no life after this one, only a contribution.
The tree gives him out again; that is the whole promise. The question 'is it the same person' is a foreign question the language does not contain.

facts.authorially_true: partial:The PATTERN survives; the MEMORY does not. Verent is right that nothing individual is recalled and wrong that nothing individual persists. The root-song is right that the promise was never memory. NEITHER source is corrected in game, and the third position — that WELLS remember what the tree forgets — is voiced only by drunks and by the Drowned Court.

facts.claim: Who cut the first sapwell, and why?
in_world_sources: The Sap and the Ledger (records only that rootkeepers refuse to say)

positions.stance: The Hist cut itself, and the keepers only keep the cut open.
The Kothringi cut the first, and the Knahaten Flu was the payment.
Nobody will say, and they become genuinely angry when pressed.

facts.notes: NO ANSWER EXISTS. Do not resolve this in any quest, book or ending. A future writer WILL want to; this flag is the refusal.

facts.claim: Were the xanmeers built by Argonians, or built by someone older and merely occupied by them?
in_world_sources: An Imperial antiquarian's survey (T1, to be written)

positions.stance: The present Argonians cannot build such things and never could; the xanmeers are the work of a vanished people whose ruins the natives inherited.
'Our grandmothers stacked the world into steps and walked up it. We do not know how.'

facts.notes: B matches hard canon CF-040/CF-041. Position A is a WRONG view held by real NPCs, and its wrongness is racial condescension. A critic must not flag A as an error — it is registered.

facts.claim: Is the Hist one mind or many trees?

positions.stance: 'The Hist' is a species. Trees are individuals, like any grove.
There is one tree. What you see are its fingers.
There was one. Some fingers have stopped listening.

facts.notes: Our resolution, chosen because canon uses both singular and plural and never adjudicates (CF-008). C preserves both usages and is the only one that leaves room for CF-009's rogue trees.

facts.claim: What caused the Knahaten Flu?
sources_real: UESP Lore:Knahaten Flu (snippet): one account blames an Argonian shaman who manipulated the spore-trees in revenge; another attributes it to natural causes. Canon does not adjudicate.
in_world_sources: An Imperial history (T7, to be written)

positions.stance: An Argonian shaman engineered it through a manipulation of the Hist, in revenge for the treatment of his people.
Natural. The marsh is full of fevers and this one travelled.

facts.authorially_true: partial:It was Hist-borne but not authored by any single person. Position A's slander is that it names a culprit; position B's evasion is that it denies the tree's involvement. NEITHER is corrected in game.
facts.notes: CANON ITSELF leaves this contradiction standing. It is the proof-of-convention for this whole registry.

facts.claim: Why has the Rootward Tide begun to fail?

positions.stance: Root-theft. The soul-gem trade intercepts the fall. Foreigners are drinking the marsh.
Too many wounds. Thirty years of Sap-Cutters opening wells for sale; the tree is bleeding capacity.
It started before the cutting and before the gem trade. Something below the Stone Wastes is filling.

facts.notes: A and B must be given GENUINELY GOOD evidence — both are real aggravations, and a player who acts on either does real good and fixes nothing. See CF-C010.

facts.claim: Legion strength in Black Marsh in 3E 427 is thin because reserves were redeployed to the Vvardenfell crisis.
In 3E 427 the Blackwood Company is a young Leyawiin outfit operating in Black Marsh, hunting for a Hist to take. It has not yet acquired the tree it is documented as holding in 3E 433.
facts.notes: Canon-compatible prequel to CF-064. Canon states no founding date (CF-065).

facts.claim: In 3E 427 there is an isolationist current in the interior — the Xul-Aneekh, 'the Deep-Kin' — a consensus, not a party, from which An-Xileel sentiment later grows. They are NEVER called the An-Xileel.
The Wet Ledger is a compact of lukiul river-factors and Imperial merchants controlling Gideon's tolls, warehouses and the Governor's debts.
The Ixtu-Vakh (Sap-Cutters) are Argonian heretics who cut sapwells for profit and sell hist-sap phials to foreigners.
The Drowned Court of Soulrest is a mixed-race mortuary order, four centuries old, that buries or burns the dead of every people for a fee.
The Blackrose Prefect runs a labour-lease scheme renting prisoners to coastal plantations and, through intermediaries, to Dres factors. Legal on paper; slavery in fact.

The Rootward Tide: everything that dies in Black Marsh leaks soul-stuff downward into a water table threaded with Hist root, which drinks it and holds it as pattern (eixa). Sap is soul in liquid form; Jel has one word, vei, for blood and sap.
facts.notes: In-world this is an Argonian IDIOM, not established Tamrielic scholarship. No foreign scholar may state it as settled.

facts.claim: A sapwell (ixtu-xul) is a Hist root deliberately cut and kept open. Wells remember what the tree forgets, because a wound is a place where something happened. This is why a well can re-issue a specific person.
facts.notes: The single constructed claim the entire checkpoint system rests on. In-world it is voiced only by drunks (per The Sap and the Ledger) and by the Drowned Court.

facts.claim: Beneath the Stone Wastes near Soulrest, a pre-Duskfall xanmeer engine built to HOLD souls is filling. It is the true cause of the Tide's failure — and the sapwells work because of it.
facts.notes: BINDING AND SECRET. No NPC may state this before the registered discovery point. Anchored in CF-042 (xanmeers as shrines in reverence and fear of Sithis). Resolving it should be able to switch off respawning — a Morrowind quest decision reaching into a Souls mechanic.

facts.claim: Sap-taint (teekh-kaoc): a non-Argonian who rests at sapwells accumulates corruption in five bands, ending in the Hist addressing them directly. At band 3 enemy SKINS lie; frames, hitboxes, telegraphs, damage and AI never change.
facts.notes: Derives directly from hard canon CF-006. Altering combat behaviour under taint is an AR-1 automatic fail.

facts.claim: Travel is by poled barge along Hist-advised routes: a poler asks the tree each morning which way the water moved in the night. Purchasable with gold, schedule-bound, refusable, severable as a plot event. Sapwells never teleport.
facts.notes: Satisfies ARBITRATION seam S7.

facts.claim: Xul-hesh (root-theft): soul-gem trapping intercepts soul-stuff that would have gone down to the roots. Argonians regard it as somewhere between poisoning a well and kidnapping, and its Daedric patron is Molag Bal.
facts.notes: Molag Bal's patronage of soul gems is canon; the Argonian reading of the trade is ours.

facts.claim: The year 3E 427 is known in interior Argonian reckoning as the Ninth Sap-Fall since the Rootless Egg. Interior Argonians count by the Hist's cycle, not the Imperial calendar.
facts.notes: An NPC who gives you an Imperial date is telling you something about themselves.
